lines.text: This number has one hundred five divisors. How many of them end in the digit one?
lines.caption: This number has one hundred five divisors. How many of them end in the digit one?

lines.text: You don't need to list them. Just watch the LAST digit.
lines.caption: You don't need to list them. Just watch the LAST digit.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this with last-digit patterns.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this with last-digit patterns.

lines.text: Here's the question. Take three to the sixth, times seven to the fourth, times thirteen squared.
lines.caption: Here's the question. Take three to the sixth, times seven to the fourth, times thirteen squared.

lines.text: How many of its positive divisors end in the digit one?
lines.caption: How many of its positive divisors end in the digit one?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Every divisor looks like three to the a, times seven to the b, times thirteen to the c.
lines.caption: Every divisor looks like three to the a, times seven to the b, times thirteen to the c.

lines.text: Here, a goes from zero to six, b from zero to four, and c from zero to two.
lines.caption: Here, a goes from zero to six, b from zero to four, and c from zero to two.

lines.text: That's seven times five times three. One hundred five divisors, way too many to list!
lines.caption: That's seven times five times three. One hundred five divisors, way too many to list!

lines.text: Good news: to find a product's last digit, you only multiply the last digits.
lines.caption: Good news: to find a product's last digit, you only multiply the last digits.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's look for a pattern. Here are the powers of three.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's look for a pattern. Here are the powers of three.

lines.text: One, three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one. Their last digits go one, three, nine, seven, repeat.
lines.caption: One, three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one. Their last digits go one, three, nine, seven, repeat.

lines.text: Powers of seven end in one, seven, nine, three, and then one again.
lines.caption: Powers of seven end in one, seven, nine, three, and then one again.

lines.text: Powers of thirteen end in one, three, nine. Thirteen acts just like three!
lines.caption: Powers of thirteen end in one, three, nine. Thirteen acts just like three!

lines.text: Now let's build a grid. Across, a goes from zero to six. Down, c goes from zero to two.
lines.caption: Now let's build a grid. Across, a goes from zero to six. Down, c goes from zero to two.

lines.text: Each of the twenty-one boxes holds the last digit of three to the a, times thirteen to the c.
lines.caption: Each of the twenty-one boxes holds the last digit of three to the a, times thirteen to the c.

lines.text: Let's find the ones. Two in the top row, one in the middle, and two at the bottom. Five in all!
lines.caption: Let's find the ones. Two in the top row, one in the middle, and two at the bottom. Five in all!

lines.text: Now bring in the sevens. Each box needs a partner from the powers of seven.
lines.caption: Now bring in the sevens. Each box needs a partner from the powers of seven.

lines.text: A box ending in one needs a partner ending in one. That's b equals zero, or four. Two ways!
lines.caption: A box ending in one needs a partner ending in one. That's b equals zero, or four. Two ways!

lines.text: A box ending in three needs a seven, because three times seven is twenty-one.
lines.caption: A box ending in three needs a seven, because three times seven is twenty-one.

lines.text: Nine needs a nine, for eighty-one. And seven needs a three, for twenty-one again.
lines.caption: Nine needs a nine, for eighty-one. And seven needs a three, for twenty-one again.

lines.text: So each of those boxes gets exactly one partner.
lines.caption: So each of those boxes gets exactly one partner.

lines.text: Five boxes end in one, with two ways each. That's ten. The other sixteen boxes add sixteen.
lines.caption: Five boxes end in one, with two ways each. That's ten. The other sixteen boxes add sixteen.

lines.text: Ten plus sixteen. So the answer is <short pause> twenty-six! Choice C.
lines.caption: Ten plus sixteen. So the answer is twenty-six! Choice C.

scenes.chapter: Solution 2: everything is a power of three

lines.text: Here's a slicker way. Three cubed is twenty-seven, and it ends in seven.
lines.caption: Here's a slicker way. Three cubed is twenty-seven, and it ends in seven.

lines.text: Seven acts like three cubed, so seven to the b acts like three to the three b.
lines.caption: Seven acts like three cubed, so seven to the b acts like three to the three b.

lines.text: Thirteen acts like three. So every divisor acts like three to the a plus three b plus c.
lines.caption: Thirteen acts like three. So every divisor acts like three to the a plus three b plus c.

lines.text: A power of three ends in one when its exponent is a multiple of four.
lines.caption: A power of three ends in one when its exponent is a multiple of four.

lines.text: So we need a plus three b plus c to be a multiple of four.
lines.caption: So we need a plus three b plus c to be a multiple of four.

lines.text: Let's go one b at a time. Here's our grid again, now filled with a plus c.
lines.caption: Let's go one b at a time. Here's our grid again, now filled with a plus c.

lines.text: When b is zero, a plus c must be zero, four, or eight. One, plus three, plus one. Five boxes.
lines.caption: When b is zero, a plus c must be zero, four, or eight. One, plus three, plus one. Five boxes.

lines.text: When b is one, three b is three. So a plus c plus three must be four or eight.
lines.caption: When b is one, three b is three. So a plus c plus three must be four or eight.

lines.text: That makes a plus c equal to one or five. Two plus three, five boxes.
lines.caption: That makes a plus c equal to one or five. Two plus three, five boxes.

lines.text: When b is two, three b is six. So a plus c is two or six. Three plus three, six boxes.
lines.caption: When b is two, three b is six. So a plus c is two or six. Three plus three, six boxes.

lines.text: When b is three, three b is nine. So a plus c is three or seven. Three plus two, five boxes.
lines.caption: When b is three, three b is nine. So a plus c is three or seven. Three plus two, five boxes.

lines.text: b equals four works just like b equals zero. Five boxes.
lines.caption: b equals four works just like b equals zero. Five boxes.

lines.text: Five plus five plus six plus five plus five. Twenty-six again!
lines.caption: Five plus five plus six plus five plus five. Twenty-six again!

lines.text: When would you pick this one? When every prime acts like a power of the same number.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? When every prime acts like a power of the same number.

lines.text: Choice A, twenty-four, is what you'd get forgetting one and the number itself. Both end in one!
lines.caption: Choice A, twenty-four, is what you'd get forgetting one and the number itself. Both end in one!

lines.text: B, twenty-five, is what you'd get if sevens always ended in one. Five boxes times five choices.
lines.caption: B, twenty-five, is what you'd get if sevens always ended in one. Five boxes times five choices.

lines.text: D, twenty-seven, is what you'd get if thirteens ended in one: nine pairs for a and b, three for c.
lines.caption: D, twenty-seven, is what you'd get if thirteens ended in one: nine pairs for a and b, three for c.

lines.text: Choice E, twenty-eight, is just too many. We checked every box, and only twenty-six work.
lines.caption: Choice E, twenty-eight, is just too many. We checked every box, and only twenty-six work.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Check each prime's last-digit cycle. Never assume it ends in one.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Check each prime's last-digit cycle. Never assume it ends in one.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same idea, new number.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same idea, new number.

lines.text: Take three to the fifth, times seven to the fourth, times thirteen cubed.
lines.caption: Take three to the fifth, times seven to the fourth, times thirteen cubed.

lines.text: How many of its positive divisors end in the digit one?
lines.caption: How many of its positive divisors end in the digit one?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Same grid! Now a goes from zero to five, and c from zero to three. That's twenty-four boxes.
lines.caption: Same grid! Now a goes from zero to five, and c from zero to three. That's twenty-four boxes.

lines.text: A box gives last digit one when a plus c is zero, four, or eight. One, plus four, plus one. Six boxes.
lines.caption: A box gives last digit one when a plus c is zero, four, or eight. One, plus four, plus one. Six boxes.

lines.text: Each of those gets two partners, b equals zero or four. That's twelve.
lines.caption: Each of those gets two partners, b equals zero or four. That's twelve.

lines.text: Twenty-four minus six leaves eighteen boxes, one partner each. That's eighteen more.
lines.caption: Twenty-four minus six leaves eighteen boxes, one partner each. That's eighteen more.

lines.text: Twelve plus eighteen. The answer is thirty!
lines.caption: Twelve plus eighteen. The answer is thirty!

lines.text: The big idea: only last digits matter, and last digits repeat in cycles.
lines.caption: The big idea: only last digits matter, and last digits repeat in cycles.

lines.text: Make each prime a power of three, for last digits. Then the exponent must be a multiple of four.
lines.caption: Make each prime a power of three, for last digits. Then the exponent must be a multiple of four.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
